context:
The NJC toy handbook's data for this scenario is as follows. The destination is Tokyo, Japan (country code JP), with in_canada_or_continental_usa false, so Module 4 (international) applies. The destination's allowance row id is D-JP-TOKYO and the traveller's accommodation is commercial. The outbound journey, in flying order, is:
- S1: MA 404, YOW to YYZ, depart local 2027-04-12T10:00 (depart UTC 14:00Z), arrive local 2027-04-12T11:10 (arrive UTC 15:10Z), in_air_minutes 70, cabins_sold [economy, business], connection_after minutes 90 with overnight_stop false.
- S2: SP 12, YYZ to HND, depart local 2027-04-12T12:40 (depart UTC 16:40Z), arrive local 2027-04-13T14:50 (arrive UTC 05:50Z), in_air_minutes 790, cabins_sold [economy, premium_economy], no connection after.
The travel-status days, earliest first, are:
- 2027-04-12: status_start_local 07:00, status_end_local null, meals_provided [dinner].
- 2027-04-13: status_start_local null, status_end_local null, meals_provided [breakfast, lunch].
- 2027-04-14: status_start_local null, status_end_local null, meals_provided [dinner].
- 2027-04-15: status_start_local null, status_end_local 18:30, meals_provided [dinner].
Each status_days entry is one calendar day in the traveller's local time; count the days as listed.
The D-JP-TOKYO allowance row (Appendix D, effective 2026-10-01) is paid in JPY. Its commercial row is breakfast 604000, lunch 660000, dinner 982000, meal_total 2246000, incidental per day 718720; its private_non_commercial row has the same meal amounts and incidental per day 449200. Use the commercial row. All amounts are integer hundredths of JPY; nothing is rounded or pro-rated.
The traveller's words (flavour only, not authoritative; the structured facts govern) are: Trade talks in Tokyo. Sakura Pacific doesn't sell business on the Toronto-Tokyo flight, so I guess the rules put me in economy the whole way; or could you just book business on another carrier? The reception dinner on the 14th is lavish, but I'd like the dinner allowance anyway. I leave home at 07:00 on the 12th.
Apply the handbook rules: cut the outbound journey at every connection whose overnight_stop is true; ordinary connections count into the block; longest_continuous_air_minutes is the largest block in minutes. A block qualifies for business only when Module 4 applies and the block is more than 540 minutes (541 qualifies, exactly 540 does not). For a qualifying segment, authorize business if the segment sells it; if business is not sold, authorize the highest class sold below business (premium_economy if sold, else economy); never move to another flight or carrier. Every other segment is economy. Meal times are breakfast 07:00, lunch 12:00, dinner 18:00 local; a meal is claimable when status_start_local <= meal time <= status_end_local, with a null start meaning status began on an earlier day and a null end meaning it continues past midnight, and only when the meal is not in meals_provided. meal_allowance_minor is the sum over all status days of the claimable meals' row amounts; incidental_allowance_minor is the number of status days times the row's incidental_minor, a part day counting as a whole day; total_minor is their sum. All times and minutes are precomputed; do no timezone arithmetic. The currency is JPY. segment_cabins must cover S1 and S2 exactly once each.
